text:
The Rangers' season turned on Oct. 9, when Igor Shesterkin injured his right knee in Washington and the team ruled him out for the year. Everything since has been about whether Dylan Garand can hold the job. The early answer is better than anyone had a right to expect: 32 saves to beat the Blues, a team that has won three straight, and 60 percent of the expected goals in those games (the quality of chances).

The organization has made its choice. James Reimer was placed on unconditional waivers for a contract termination, Sean Durzi went on injured reserve, and Tye Kartye, a waiver claim from Seattle, keeps earning minutes, with the New York Post writing that he's making every one count. Recent lineups have had Joonas Korpisalo back as the other goalie.

At 10-7-1, New York is a coin flip for the playoffs in our simulations (54 percent). The process is fine, 53 percent of the five-on-five chances, and the Mika Zibanejad, Alexis Lafrenière and Gabe Perreault line has outscored teams 7-4. The shooters have scored about six fewer goals than expected, so there's offense to come. The question is how long a goalie who started the season in the minors can carry this. If he can, the Rangers are a playoff team. If he can't, nothing else here fixes it.
headline: The Rangers are playing for Dylan Garand now
